target_customer: Non-technical workers and small teams that need answers from a database without writing SQL, paying monthly per plan
problem: Business users depend on analysts or engineers for ad hoc data questions. Shape answers plain English questions against a database and returns SQL backed answers and charts.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription tiers ($49 Starter, $499 Team, custom Enterprise per the company site)
product_category: AI data analyst, natural language to SQL

founders.name: Namit Chadha
founders.background_notes: The YC page calls him a repeat founder but names no earlier company. Source: YC company page.

technical_complexity.rationale: In 2021 reliable natural language to SQL needed custom semantic handling and was hard to make accurate, but a 4 person team could build a Slack based wrapper over customer databases. No source describes the original architecture.

defensibility.rationale: No data, network or integration moat is described by any source. The later arrival of general purpose language models made the wedge copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source documents what incumbents did. Many text to SQL products appeared after 2022, per roundup articles dated 2025 and 2026.

market_need_then: The YC one liner frames the pain as workers lacking SQL access to data. No dated 2021 source quantifying demand was found.

branding.domain_note: Uses shape.xyz. Whoxy lists the domain creation date as 2014 and a GoDaddy registrar; no purchase story found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and benefit led: 'Data on demand' and 'Your AI data analyst' on the company site

brand_strength.rationale: Generic common word on a .xyz domain, easily confused with other companies called Shape or Shaped; search results for the name were dominated by unrelated firms. No community or press about the brand found.

outcome_analysis: Shape remains active as a very small team with a niche AI data analyst product. No funding beyond a possible small YC note, no acquisition and no layoffs were found. The name is generic and the category became crowded after language models improved, so the company's trajectory is unclear rather than a recorded success or failure.
notes: A CB Insights snippet reported a $0.5M convertible note from Y Combinator dated 2021-01-01 (probably approximate). It is a single aggregator figure and is unverified, so it is not recorded as a round. Search results mixed Shape with Shaped, Shapes and Shapeways, which are different companies. Dealroom lists a 'shape inc' as acquired but could not be linked to this company. No competitor source dated near the 2021 batch was found, so the list is empty; the YC launch post found for this query turned out to belong to camelAI.
